newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Congressman admitting campaign finance violations.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Congressman admitting campaign finance violations.

text.p: Republican Rep.Jay Kim, the first Korean-American elected to the U.S. Congress, has agreed to plead guilty to accepting illegal campaign contributions, federal prosecutors said on Thursday.

U.S. Attorney Nora Manella said Kim's wife June and his campaign committee had also been charged with the campaign finance violations that include accepting donations from corporations and from a foreigner.
Kim and his wife will appear in court on Monday to enter their pleas, Manella said. Kim will also plead guilty on behalf of the Jay Kim for Congress Committee of concealing illegal contributions.

"The charges ... demonstrate that Congressman Kim, his wife and his campaign committee, over a period of years, knowingly and wilfully disregarded the campaign finance laws applicable to all candidates for federal office," Manella said in a statement.
"Congressman Kim and his wife have acknowledged their criminal conduct and accepted responsibility for it," the statement said.

Kim, a three-term Republican from California, faces up to three years in prison and fines up to three times the amount of the illegal contributions. But a spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's office said it would recommend no more than six months, although the judge would have the final say.
The spokesman said the three counts Kim was pleading guilty to and the two his wife was admitting, were misdemeanors. As such Kim was unlikely to lose his seat in the House of Representatives.
If they were felonies, he might face expulsion from the House.

Kim agreed to plead guilty to three counts -- accepting an illegal $50,000 campaign contribution from a Taiwanese citizen, contributing more that $83,000 in illegal corporate contributions from JayKim Engineers Inc. to his campaign and accepting an illegal $12,000 corporate contribution from Nikko Enterprises Inc.
June Kim will plead guilty to two counts for accepting more than $19,000 in illegal corporate contributions.
Jay Kim will plead guilty on behalf of the campaign committee to five felony counts of concealing illegal contributions of over $200,000.

The U.S. Attorney's office previously obtained convictions against five multinational corporations which made illegal campaign contributions to Kim's 1992 campaign. Korean Airlines, Hyundai Motor America, Samsung America, Daewoo International America and Haitai America have paid a total of $1.6 million in fines.
